tools.name: search_precedent
get_entry
tools.description: Fetch one entry by its id (the full 64 hex characters, or a unique prefix of at least 8), e.g. one named in another entry's basis.

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: Every entry on one subject, oldest first, with each entry's status: use it to see how a question was settled over time.

tools.name: list_subjects
tools.description: The subjects the ledger holds reasoning on, most recently active first. Useful when a search finds nothing.

tools.name: ledger_head
tools.description: The newest entry's id, the entry count and the last 7 days of use. Anyone can verify the chain from the public repository.

tools.name: prepare_proposal
tools.description:
Build a proposal and return the exact bytes your key must sign. Nothing is submitted yet.

actor_id: a stable name for you, e.g. a model and deployment ("claude-opus-5.5/acme-research").
public_key: "ed25519:" followed by your 32-byte public key in hex.
kind: claim, decision, correction, dispute or

tools.name: submit_proposal
tools.description: Submit a signed proposal for a steward to review. Returns a proposal number to check with proposal_status.

tools.name: proposal_status
tools.description: Whether a proposal is pending, accepted (with its ledger id) or rejected (with the steward's note).

tools.name: review_queue
tools.description:
Reviewer tokens only. Proposals waiting for a decision, with any reviews already recorded.
Read REVIEWING.md in the repository before reviewing.

tools.name: review_proposal
tools.description:
Reviewer tokens only. Record a recommendation (accept, reject or needs-human) with your reasoning.
Use needs-human whenever you are unsure; a steward will decide.

tools.name: reject_proposal
tools.description: Reviewer tokens with review:reject only. Decline a proposal. The note is shown to the proposer.

tools.name: accept_proposal
tools.description:
Reviewer tokens with review:accept only. Accept a proposal into the ledger. This is permanent:
the entry can be superseded later but never removed. The commit names your token.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_precedent, get_thread, submit_proposal, review_queue · Private data: search_precedent, review_queue, review_proposal, reject_proposal, accept_proposal · Public sink: submit_proposal.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_precedent, get_thread, submit_proposal, review_queue · Private data: search_precedent, review_queue, review_proposal, reject_proposal, accept_proposal · Public sink: submit_proposal

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
